messages:
rohit: heads-up — canary embeddings p95 creeping up, deploybot flagged it at 4623456775 :alert:
deploybot: [signal] embed-canary p95=685ms (threshold=600ms); trend=up; autorevert=false.
clare: saw a correlated increase in `kvcache.miss_rate` +10% and a few `quant-fallback` traces. Possibly the new quant patch.
jules: If it's quantization fallout, safest to revert. Manual rollback for canary then pin dedicated pools.
rohit: Agreed. Ops runbook: if p95>threshold for 10m OR error-rate rising, do manual rollback.
ops-oncall-bot: runbook link: https://go/redwood/runbooks/rollback — escalate if >30m or customer impact >0.5%.
clare: I'll pause the canary traffic and prepare the revert.
[deploybot] action: `pause-rollout --target=canary-embeds --by=clare`
clare: paused.
[deploybot] action: `rollout revert --target=canary-embeds --to-version=v3.4.2 --staged=3 --operator=clare`
deploybot: stage 1/3 succeeded. p95 -> 360ms on affected host.
jules: pinning dedicated pools to v3.4.2 to avoid re-scheduling the bumped image: `service.pin('embedders', 'v3.4.2')` done.
rohit: good. Monitor for 15m then resume. I'll draft a short release-note blurb: "Reverted canary due to temporary perf regression; investigating quantization change."
ops-oncall-bot: created incident I-2026-0912 for tracking. Postmortem owner: clare.
clare: action items for postmortem: 1) revert quant patch from CI until tests added, 2) add kv warmup shim in rollout, 3) add canary gating on kv-hit >= 92%.
deploybot: metadata updated: release_state=reverted, pinned_version=v3.4.2, operator=clare
jules: customer-comm draft ready in #cust-comms — short & factual.
rohit: monitoring window open. If stable, we'll leave release pinned and schedule a safe re-release after fixes. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
note: Manual, staged rollback executed for canary embeds; dedicated pools pinned; incident created and postmortem tasks assigned.
